headline: Senate Impeachment Court Subpoenas Baste Duterte for September 23 Appearance
seoTitle: Baste Duterte Subpoenaed in Sara Duterte Impeachment Trial | FMB News
seoDescription: The Senate impeachment court has subpoenaed Davao City Mayor Sebastian 'Baste' Duterte and other witnesses to appear on September 23 in Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial.
deck: The court directed Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte and other witnesses to appear on September 23. A subpoena compels appearance or production of evidence; it is not a finding of wrongdoing.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Senate impeachment court issued a subpoena directing Davao City Mayor Sebastian 'Baste' Duterte to appear on September 23 in the impeachment trial of his sister, Vice President Sara Duterte.

Philippine News Agency reported that Duterte and four others were ordered to appear. ABS-CBN News, GMA News and the Philippine Daily Inquirer independently reported the subpoena involving the Davao City mayor.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: GMA News reported that House prosecutors want to ask Duterte, in his capacity as Davao City mayor, about whether the city government had dealings with Gencorp Industries Inc., a company prosecutors have linked to the vice president.

That asserted link is part of the prosecution's case and is not presented here as an independently established finding. The subpoena itself does not establish wrongdoing by Sebastian Duterte, Vice President Duterte, the company, or any other person.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: The court issued the subpoena and directed the witnesses to appear on September 23. Gerardo del Rosario, director of the Securities and Exchange Commission's company registration and monitoring department, was among the other people identified in independent reporting as subpoenaed.

sections.heading: What remains unresolved
paragraphs: The substance of the witnesses' eventual testimony, whether every subpoenaed witness will appear, and what weight the senator-judges will give any resulting evidence remain unresolved.
The impeachment allegations against Vice President Duterte remain contested and have not been finally adjudicated by the Senate impeachment court.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The subpoena was issued at the end of Day 26 of the impeachment proceedings, during which retired Supreme Court justices also presented differing legal views concerning the vote threshold for conviction. FMB News reported those threshold arguments separately because they concern a distinct procedural question.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The court has scheduled further proceedings for September 23. Watch for service and compliance with the subpoenas, any testimony admitted by the court, and the separate oral arguments over the disputed conviction-vote threshold.

verificationNotes: Philippine News Agency reports that the Senate impeachment court subpoenaed Sebastian Duterte and four others.
ABS-CBN News independently reported the subpoena and updated its report at 6:15 p.m. PHT.
GMA News independently reported at 10:31 p.m. PHT that the court ordered Sebastian Duterte to testify and attributed the prosecution's intended subject of questioning.
The Philippine Daily Inquirer independently reported the issuance of the subpoenas.
The article treats prosecution assertions as attributed allegations and explicitly states that a subpoena is not a finding of wrongdoing.

The hero is a 2022 PCOO file photograph hosted by Wikimedia Commons. Commons identifies PCOO as author and marks the work public domain in the Philippines under PD-PhilippinesGov. The caption explicitly states that it does not depict the September 16 proceedings.
